quests.instruction: Try this sentence: 'I have 3 pens and 2 books.' Mix the numbers and words carefully.
quests.question: I have 3 pens and 2 books.
quests.hint: Capital I, 'have', the number 3, 'pens' (tail on p), 'and', the number 2, 'books'. Keep each number the same height as a capital.
quests.explanation: Numbers and words share one line, so they need the same baseline. Leave a normal gap on either side of each number.
quests.funFact: In place-value numbers, a digit's worth depends on where it sits, so the 3 in 30 is worth ten times the 3 in 3.

quests.instruction: Write 'We have 25 students in our class.' on one neat line.
quests.question: We have 25 students in our class.
quests.correctAnswer: We have 25 students in our class.
quests.hint: Capital W, 'e have', the two-digit number 25 with the digits close together, then 'students in our class.' End with a full stop.
quests.explanation: A two-digit number should look like one number. Keep its digits close, and leave a gap on either side.
quests.funFact: The philosopher Plato founded a famous school in Athens called the Academy around 387 BCE.

quests.instruction: Write the sentence 'The bus comes at 7:30.' Include the time with a colon.
quests.question: The bus comes at 7:30.
quests.hint: Capital T, 'he', 'bus' (tall b), 'comes', 'at', then 7, colon, 30, and a full stop right after the 0.
quests.explanation: A sentence can end with a number. The full stop comes right after the last digit, sitting on the baseline.
quests.funFact: School buses are painted yellow in many countries, because yellow is easy to see.

quests.instruction: Write the message 'Please bring your lunch box tomorrow.'
quests.question: Please bring your lunch box tomorrow.
quests.correctAnswer: Please bring your lunch box tomorrow.
quests.hint: Capital P, then the other five words. Check the gaps between words and keep the line level. Full stop at the end.
quests.explanation: A sentence a teacher might really send home. Planning the line first keeps the gaps even.
quests.funFact: In Mumbai, delivery workers called dabbawalas bring many thousands of home-cooked lunches to offices every day.

quests.instruction: Write the message 'Thank you for helping me today.'
quests.question: Thank you for helping me today.
quests.correctAnswer: Thank you for helping me today.
quests.hint: Think in two chunks: 'Thank you for' and 'helping me today.' Tails on y, p, g and y should all be about the same length.
quests.explanation: Six words with many tails and tall letters. Check the heights as you go.
quests.funFact: In Japanese, 'thank you' is 'arigato'.

quests.instruction: Write the message 'Sorry, I am late.' Put a comma after Sorry.
quests.question: Sorry, I am late.
quests.hint: Capital S, 'orry' (tail on y), comma, gap, capital I, 'am late.' Both capitals should be the same height.
quests.explanation: A comma after the first word gives a pause. Then a second capital for the word 'I'.
quests.funFact: Clock hands move clockwise because early sundials cast shadows that moved in that direction in the northern half of the world.

quests.instruction: Write a shopping list with a title: 'Shopping list: tea, sugar, bread'.
quests.question: Shopping list: tea, sugar, bread
quests.hint: Write the title 'Shopping list', add a colon straight after it, then the items with commas between them. The g's and p's go below the baseline.
quests.explanation: A title with a colon introduces the list. Then commas separate each item.
quests.funFact: The word 'list' once meant the edge of a piece of cloth.

quests.instruction: Write a packing list: 'Pack: shirt, socks, towel'.
quests.question: Pack: shirt, socks, towel
quests.hint: Capital P, 'ack', colon, gap, 'shirt' comma, 'socks' comma, 'towel'. Remember: tall stems (k, h, l) reach the top line.
quests.explanation: A colon and two commas give the list its shape. Keep them small and close to the words.
quests.funFact: Suitcases with wheels were first sold widely in the 1970s.

quests.instruction: Write a to-do list: 'To do: read, draw, play'.
quests.question: To do: read, draw, play
quests.hint: Write 'To do' and a colon. Then three jobs, each followed by a comma except the last. d, d and l are tall; p and y have tails.
quests.explanation: Short words in a list. Keep all the commas the same size and all the gaps equal.
quests.funFact: Many people find that crossing finished jobs off a list feels good and helps them keep going.

quests.instruction: Write the instruction 'Wash your hands with soap.'
quests.question: Wash your hands with soap.
quests.hint: Five words, many tall letters. In 'Wash your hands with soap', h, d, h and t rise up and y and p drop down. The full stop sits on the baseline.
quests.explanation: A real health instruction. Keep the line straight and the words evenly spaced.
quests.funFact: Washing your hands with soap for about twenty seconds helps to remove germs.

quests.instruction: Write the instruction 'Add two cups of water.'
quests.question: Add two cups of water.
quests.hint: Capital A, 'dd', 'two', 'cups' (tail on p), 'of', 'water'. Cross the t's at the same height. Full stop.
quests.explanation: A recipe-style instruction. The tall t's in 'two' and 'water' should be the same height.
quests.funFact: Water is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom, which is why its formula is H2O.

quests.instruction: Write the instruction 'Close the door gently.'
quests.question: Close the door gently.
quests.hint: Capital C, 'lose', 'the', 'door', 'gently' with tails on g and y. Full stop.
quests.explanation: Four words with tails at the end. Leave space under the line for g and y.
quests.funFact: Revolving doors were invented in 1888.

quests.instruction: Write the first step: 'Step 1: Wash the rice.'
quests.question: Step 1: Wash the rice.
quests.hint: Capital S, 'tep', gap, the number 1, colon, gap, capital W, 'ash the rice.' Check the 1 is as tall as the capitals.
quests.explanation: Step numbers are part of the instruction. The number, the colon, and the capital letter all need to be clear.
quests.funFact: Rinsing rice washes off some of the extra starch on the grains.

quests.instruction: Write the second step: 'Step 2: Add water.'
quests.question: Step 2: Add water.
quests.hint: Capital S, 'tep', the number 2, colon, then capital A, 'dd water.' Keep your 2 tall, with a flat base.
quests.explanation: A step list uses the same pattern each time: Step, number, colon, then the instruction.
quests.funFact: At sea level, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

quests.instruction: Write the third step: 'Step 3: Cook for ten minutes.'
quests.question: Step 3: Cook for ten minutes.
quests.hint: Capital S, 'tep', the number 3, colon, capital C, 'ook for ten minutes.' Check the two m's and the dot on i.
quests.explanation: A longer step with many small letters. Keep the letters even and the gaps equal.
quests.funFact: Heat makes dry rice grains soak up water and become soft.

quests.instruction: Write today's date as a sentence: 'Today is Friday, 2 October.'
quests.question: Today is Friday, 2 October.
quests.hint: Write 'Today is', then the day with a capital F. The comma follows 'Friday' right away. Then the number 2 and a capital O. The tails on y go below.
quests.explanation: The day and month names always start with a capital. The number goes between the comma and the month.
quests.funFact: October comes from the Latin word for eight, because it was the eighth month in the old Roman calendar.

quests.instruction: Write: 'My birthday is on 5 March.'
quests.question: My birthday is on 5 March.
quests.hint: Write 'My birthday is on', then the number 5, then the month with a capital M. The number should be as tall as the capital letters.
quests.explanation: A month name gets a capital, even in the middle of a sentence.
quests.funFact: Aquamarine, a pale blue-green gem, is the birthstone for March in many lists.

quests.instruction: Write: 'School ends on 20 April.'
quests.question: School ends on 20 April.
quests.hint: Write 'School ends on', then 20 with the digits close together, then a capital A and 'pril'. The full stop comes right after the l.
quests.explanation: A sentence that ends with a date. Keep the digits in 20 close together.
quests.funFact: The calendar we use today was introduced by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582.

quests.instruction: Write the greeting of a letter: 'Dear Grandma,'
quests.question: Dear Grandma,
quests.hint: Capital D, 'ear', gap, capital G, 'randma' (tall d), then the comma right after the a.
quests.explanation: A letter begins with 'Dear' and the person's name, both with capitals, and then a comma.
quests.funFact: The first postage stamp, the Penny Black, was issued in Britain in 1840.

quests.instruction: Write the middle of a letter: 'Thank you for the lovely gift.'
quests.question: Thank you for the lovely gift.
quests.correctAnswer: Thank you for the lovely gift.
quests.hint: Write 'Thank you for' first, then 'the lovely gift.' Both l's in 'lovely' and the f in 'gift' are tall. Close each circle.
quests.explanation: A full sentence in the middle of a letter. The tall letters make a skyline, so keep them at the same height.
quests.funFact: The letters PS at the end of a letter stand for 'postscript', from Latin words for 'written after'.

quests.instruction: Write the closing of a letter: 'Love, Maya'
quests.question: Love, Maya
quests.hint: Write 'Love' with a capital L, put the comma right after the e, then add your name on the same line, starting with a capital M.
quests.explanation: A letter ends with a word like 'Love' and the writer's name, with a comma after the closing word.
quests.funFact: The ancient Romans often ended letters with the word 'vale', which means 'be well'.

quests.instruction: Write a two-sentence message: 'I am at the park. Please come soon!'
quests.question: I am at the park. Please come soon!
quests.correctAnswer: I am at the park. Please come soon!
quests.hint: First sentence: capital I and a full stop. Second sentence: capital P and an exclamation mark. Leave a slightly wider gap between them.
quests.explanation: Different endings for different feelings: the full stop is calm and the exclamation mark is urgent.
quests.funFact: Public parks became common in many cities in the 1800s.

quests.instruction: Write: 'The bus is late. I will walk.'
quests.question: The bus is late. I will walk.
quests.correctAnswer: The bus is late. I will walk.
quests.hint: Two sentences, two full stops. After 'late.' leave a wider gap, then start with a capital I. Keep the tall letters in 'bus', 'late' and 'walk' level.
quests.explanation: Two short sentences with lots of tall letters. Keep their tops the same height.
quests.funFact: The word 'bus' is short for 'omnibus', a Latin word meaning 'for everyone'.

quests.instruction: Write: 'We won the match! It was fun.'
quests.question: We won the match! It was fun.
quests.correctAnswer: We won the match! It was fun.
quests.hint: Put the exclamation mark right after 'match', leave a wider gap, and begin 'It' with a capital I. End with a full stop after 'fun'.
quests.explanation: A celebration, then a calm sentence. Both marks are important, so make them clear.
quests.funFact: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896.

quests.instruction: Copy this saying about learning: 'Practice makes perfect.'
quests.question: Practice makes perfect.
quests.hint: Write 'Practice', 'makes' and 'perfect' on a level baseline. The double c's are round, and the f needs room above the line.
quests.explanation: Three words, one capital and one full stop. Keep the letters even from start to end.
quests.funFact: Proverbs are short sayings that pass advice from one generation to the next.

quests.instruction: Copy this saying from an old story: 'Slow and steady wins the race.'
quests.question: Slow and steady wins the race.
quests.correctAnswer: Slow and steady wins the race.
quests.hint: Count six words as you write: Slow, and, steady, wins, the, race. Keep the tall d's, t's and h's even, and let the y in 'steady' drop below.
quests.explanation: A six-word sentence. Take a breath and keep the baseline straight.
quests.funFact: This saying comes from the fable of the tortoise and the hare, which is credited to Aesop of ancient Greece.

quests.instruction: Copy this famous saying: 'A journey of a thousand miles begins with one step.'
quests.question: A journey of a thousand miles begins with one step.
quests.correctAnswer: A journey of a thousand miles begins with one step.
quests.hint: Capital A, then the other nine words, ending with a full stop. If you run out of room, continue on the next line at a word break.
quests.explanation: A long sentence is a real test: gaps, heights and tails must all stay steady to the final full stop.
quests.funFact: This saying is often credited to Lao Tzu, a Chinese philosopher.

quests.instruction: Copy the sentence that uses every letter of the alphabet: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.'
quests.question: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
quests.correctAnswer: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
quests.hint: Nine words, one capital, one full stop. If you need to, split it into two lines after 'fox'. Watch tails on q, j, p, y, g.
quests.explanation: This sentence uses all 26 letters, so it tests the entire alphabet you have learned.
quests.funFact: Sentences like this one were used to test typewriters and printing machines.

quests.instruction: Write a note to your teacher: 'Dear teacher, thank you for helping me learn to write.'
quests.question: Dear teacher, thank you for helping me learn to write.
quests.correctAnswer: Dear teacher, thank you for helping me learn to write.
quests.hint: Capital D, a comma after 'teacher', then the rest of the sentence in small letters, with a full stop at the end. Mind the gaps.
quests.explanation: A real note, in your own handwriting. Capital, comma, steady size, steady gaps, and a full stop.
quests.funFact: Writing was invented independently in several places, including Mesopotamia, China and Mesoamerica.

quests.instruction: Write your final sentence: 'I can write letters, numbers, words and sentences. I am a writer!'
quests.question: I can write letters, numbers, words and sentences. I am a writer!
quests.correctAnswer: I can write letters, numbers, words and sentences. I am a writer!
quests.hint: Two sentences: capital I, full stop after 'sentences'. Capital I and exclamation mark at the end. Commas after 'letters', 'numbers' and 'words'.
quests.explanation: Strokes became letters, letters became words, and words became sentences. Everything you practiced is in this line.
quests.funFact: Handwriting has been used by people for about five thousand years.
